assumptions.clearance_source: SpanGuard demo table. Not a regulatory standard: replace with the utility's own rules.
assumptions.note: Demo clearance values and assumed conductor data; not an engineering assessment.

fall_in.method: Tree tops are local maxima of a canopy height model; a tree can strike a wire when the nearest point of any simulated wire lies within its height plus a lean allowance of its base.

priority.method: score = (clearance + probability + grow-in + fall-in + clash + air gap + consequence points) x voltage weight. Clearance: violation 40, watch 20. Probability: 30 x P(violation) from Monte Carlo. Grow-in (not yet breached): <=1 yr 15, <=3 yr 10, <=5 yr 5. Fall-in: 15 per strike tree (max 30), 5 per watch tree (max 10). Clash: violation 20, watch 10. Tower air gap: violation 20, watch 10. Consequence: points of the consequence polygons the span crosses (highest per layer). Voltage weight: 1 + kV/400.

air_gap.method: Suspension strings swing by the insulator swing angle in every wind case; the swung conductor end is checked against the tower's own LiDAR points. Required gap: the phase-earth value of the clash rules (demo values, not regulatory).

rating.temp_note: Clearance never limits up to 150 °C; the conductor's thermal limit governs.
rating.wind_note: Clearance holds up to the 1500 Pa search limit.

air_gap.note: Not judged at T02: wire-class hardware there suggests a tension tower (no string swing). Confirm the structure type.

ampacity.note: Per-phase current for one conductor; assumed resistance, emissivity and absorptivity (see Assumptions).

spans.note: Edge span: the far tower is outside the survey, so only survey-condition clearance is reported.

grow_in.note: no breach within 10 m of growth
